ready_to_post_reply.body:
Two things cost you the most in a diminished value claim, and both are avoidable.

First, evidence structure. The itemised repair invoice matters more than the total. Carriers discount cosmetic work and pay more where structural, safety or ADAS/calibration lines appear, so a single total line reads as cosmetic even when it wasn't. Pull the itemised invoice and point at the parts/labour split.

Second, comparables beat formulas. Most carriers quote the same 10%-of-damage approach adjusted for age and mileage. The NAIC notes it grew out of one Georgia Supreme Court case and has no legal basis elsewhere, and that it can double-count mileage because mileage is already priced into standard values. You can use that number to sanity-check a lowball. You cannot use it as your evidence - an adjuster can discount a formula. What they cannot easily discount is a valuation of your exact year, trim and mileage in clean condition versus with the accident reported, ideally backed by a dealer or trade-in letter in dollars.

One practical note: decide when you plan to sell. An insurer's strongest argument is that the loss is unrealised if you keep the car. Saying you are trading it within a stated timeframe, and backing that with actual trade offers, removes most of that argument.

Also ask them, in writing, to show the calculation behind their figure. They often are not required to, but the request often moves the offer anyway.

I put the whole method - eligibility check first, document order, the comparables approach, and the release trap worth knowing about - on a free page here: https://galaxyaek7-del.github.io/openclaw-factory/customer_site/guide-diminished-value-claim.html

I also sell a $59 kit that packages the forms (eligibility matrix, demand letter skeleton, evidence and negotiation log). Galaxy Forge has 0 sales and no reviews, and nothing here is legal advice or an appraisal service - check whether it is worth $59 for your situation rather than taking my word for it.
